content: Phenazone, also known as phenazon, is a pharmaceutical compound classified as an analgesic, meaning it is used to relieve pain. It is synthesized through two primary methods: one involves the reduction of diortho-dinitrodiphenyl using sodium amalgam and methyl alcohol, while the other involves heating diphenylene-ortho-dihydrazine with hydrochloric acid at a temperature of 150°C. The resulting compound crystallizes into needle-like structures that have a melting point of 156°C. When exposed to potassium permanganate, phenazone undergoes oxidation, resulting in the formation of pyridazine tetracarboxylic acid. Phenazone is also known by several synonyms, including Analgesine, Antipyrine, Diméthyloxyquinazine, Oxydiméthylquinazine, Oxydiméthylquinizine, and Pyrazoline.
